To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

short-term intravenous infusion of soybean-based lipid emulsion (10%) in sheep resulted in an increase in triglyceride and glucose concentrations and a decrease in insulin and magnesium concentrations.

short term infusion of a lipid emulsion in healthy ewes resulted in a significant elevation of blood triglycerides, a significant reduction of insulin concentrations and an increase in insulin resistance (Homa-IR) index, which returned to baseline values within 6 hr after infusion.

intravenous infusion of soybean based lipid (lipid) emulsion (LE) temporarily increased blood triglyceride (TG) and glucose (Glu) concentrations, decreased insulin (Ins) and magnesium (Mg) concentrations and increased homeostasis model assessment of Ins resistance (HOMAR-IR) values, indicating a state of Ins resistance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a soybean-based lipid emulsion (10%) on some metabolic parameters in sheep.
the use of lipid based emulsified fat in ruminants.
the effect of intravenously infused lipid emulsion in sheep, which has been poorly investigated.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intravenous infusion of soybean based lipid infusion temporarily influences some blood constituents.
Lipovenoes can be safely used intravenously in sheep, but its use in sheep should be carefully considered in cases of insulin resistance.
intravenous infusion of soybean based lipid based emulsification is safe in ruminants and it does not induce any adverse effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

intravenous infusion of soybean oil based lipid emulsion in clinically healthy sheep resulted in a significant decrease in the insulin concentrations, increase in the triglyceride, calcium, phosphorous and glucose concentrations and a significant increase in HOMR-IR values at timepoints two and four hr after infusion.
Lipovenoes is a safe intravenous lipid emulsion for use in ruminants and that it can be used to improve nutritional support for sick animals.
the intravenous infusion of LE resulted in a significant change of some blood constituents in clinically healthy sheep.
The main takeaway from our work is that
lipid emulsions can safely be used in ruminant patients not suffering from extensive fat mobilization.
the infusion of lipid emulsions should be done with caution, particularly when animals are in a state of negative energy balance.
intravenous infusion of lipid emulsion temporarily influenced some blood parameters in sheep, and that the effects were transient and not associated with any adverse clinical signs.
